title: Peer maturity, write-loss, and consumer gate crosswalk
mode: Deeper/broader primary-source research and plan-only implementation crosswalk
scope: Compare maturity evidence and failure dispositions across independent DWG/DXF implementations
Reconcile ACadSharp no-op writer/native AUDIT and solid-writer reports with local graph and carrier gates
Distinguish DXF version reassignment/export behavior from actual version conversion
Separate raw ASM/ACIS carrier delivery, OGR projection, B-rep semantics, and native FreeCAD import
Cross-check the LibreDWG R2004 decompressor security mechanism against the current local page decoder

method.kind: Primary repository documentation/issues plus read-only local source audit
method.limitations: Mutable upstream documentation/source and issue pages were reviewed as published on 2026-10-18. ACadSharp #1277 contains private-file observations and no public DWG fixture; peer reports are implementation-specific, not normative format authorities. The local decompressor review was source inspection only, not fuzzing or sanitizer execution. ODA v5.4.1 remains authoritative for DWG byte layout.

sources.revision: 0.14.1 release notes and mutable master source/docs accessed 2026-10-18
sources.observed: NEWS records security/data-loss fixes for R2004 decompressor buffer accounting, section page-map bounds, allocation arithmetic, object lifetime, and progress. objects.in distinguishes STABLE, UNSTABLE, and DEBUGGING class states; the manual separately lists unhandled classes and classes without R2018 test coverage. These signals are scoped maturity evidence, not blanket version or semantic qualification.

sources.revision: Issue bodies and mutable issue index accessed 2026-10-18
sources.observed: Issue #1277 reports ACadSharp 3.7.16 no-op AC1032 DWG writer output rejected by AutoCAD LT 2026 AUDIT, with standalone MLEADER context objects removed; the report says two serialization changes were jointly needed on two private drawings and provides no public fixture. Issue #1195 separately reports 3DSOLID/REGION omission on a DWG-to-DXF writer route. Neither report establishes a local defect or every current peer release behavior.

DXFEntity export documentation says unsupported features of the selected DXF version may be ignored and that ezdxf does not convert between versions. ACIS tools support selected SAT/SAB parse/export profiles and reject unsupported structures; mesh conversion is bounded and does not provide a general ACIS kernel.

The AC1027+ DXF extensible mode exposes raw ASMData and ASMTransform, while the documentation explicitly says ASM entities cannot be converted to OGR geometries by this driver. Projection/tessellation remains a separate, lossy route.

The DWG route converts through an external converter to DXF and then uses a selected DXF importer. Converter status, output existence, import success, visible 2D result, and 3D shape construction are distinct outcomes.

sources.revision: Workspace source at baseline de27a3391a624aba03ca71f3583c4b3a6e6396a9 plus existing user changes
sources.observed: dwgReader18::parseDataPage uses bounded preflighted section storage and page-local decompression windows; the inspected code does not have LibreDWG's cited mutable live-buffer shrink shape. Existing PAR-14/PAR-26 owners cover related capacity/arithmetic/range controls. This is static review, not a sanitizer or exhaustive malformed-stream proof.

assessment.planImpact: Refines the existing composed comparator gate: bind implementation/profile/version/direction, map source identity and ownership to an explicit output disposition, separate raw ACIS/ASM carrier and association from parsed B-rep semantics, and distinguish peer self-read from independent/native acceptance. Existing PAR/7* owners remain responsible; no new finding or local implementation task was justified.
